name: C-130J Super Hercules
summary: Modernized four-turboprop tactical airlifter with glass cockpit and new engines, flown by the Air Force, Marine Corps and Coast Guard in transport, tanker, special-operations and rescue versions.

wings: High-mounted straight wing with tapered outer panels
KC-130J, HC-130J and MC-130J carry hose-and-drogue refueling pods under the outer wings
engines: Four turboprops with six-blade, curved scimitar propellers
Slimmer engine nacelles than older Hercules models
fuselage: Wide, boxy fuselage with upswept tail, rear ramp and landing-gear sponsons
No eyebrow windows above the cockpit windscreen
Variants add a refueling probe over the cockpit (MC/HC), side-firing guns (AC-130J) or a stretched fuselage (-30)
tail: Tall single vertical fin with a dorsal fillet
Large horizontal tail at the top of the upswept rear fuselage

tellTales: Six-blade curved scimitar propellers on a four-turboprop
High-winged boxy transport with upswept tail, rear ramp and gear sponsons
Plain cockpit windscreen with no small windows above it

confusedWith.howToTell: The C-130J has six-blade curved scimitar props and no eyebrow windows; the C-130H has four-blade paddle props (or straight eight-blade props) and eyebrow windows over the cockpit.
The C-130J is a smaller four-turboprop with propellers; the C-17 is a much larger four-jet with a T-tail and winglets.
